name: Nations & the believer
about: God's judgment on nations, and the believer in them.

teachings.title: The evil of sodomites given free reign
teachings.summary: The Gibeah outrage parallels Sodom to show the evil of a nation allowing sodomites free reign, which God's law calls an abomination worthy of death.
teachings.text:
*And it came to pass in those days, when there was no king in Israel*...and we know, men did what was right in their own eyes.

**Judges 19** begins another tale of the excesses and depravity that Israel fell into absent a Moses or Joshua. Relying on regional judges to come forth by God to deliver them from the results that came from the abominations they fell into.

This channel has covered the story told in **Judges 19-21** before, because it deals directly with the evil of allowing sodomites free reign in a nation.

The parallel to **Genesis 19** and the story of the destruction of Sodom is meant to drive home the point. Parallelism is God's way of signifying the importance of the message He is conveying.

A mob of baser fellows of the lewd sort, sons of Belial, Sodomites, surround a house in a city they are allowed free reign in, and there demand the master of the house deliver up a stranger, a man, that they may know him. These dogs burn with lust one for another, working that which is unseemly. Men with men, laying together. Abominations.

Worse they seek to force it by violence, in a mob. To a stranger, a sojourner. A Levite, of the priesthood.

None of the law or the things of God mattered to these reprobates, not retaining Him in their minds. Their conscience seared with a hot iron. Being twice-dead, fit to be burned.

**Leviticus 18:22**
*Thou shalt not lie with mankind, as with womankind: it is abomination.*

**Leviticus 20:13**
*If a man also lie with mankind, as he lieth with a woman, both of them have committed an abomination: they shall surely be put to death; their blood shall be upon them.*

**Deuteronomy 23:17**
*There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel.*

**Romans 1:29-32**
*being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.*

teachings.title: Nations judged for shedding innocent blood
teachings.summary: A nation that refuses to punish those who shed innocent blood, whether by repealing capital punishment, funding abortion or bombing innocents, is guilty of that blood and God will judge it, so believers must stand against it.
teachings.text:
**Deuteronomy 21** ramps up the commands of God in this, Moses giving of the law prior to entering the promised land. The land given as an inheritance to the children of Israel, if they maintain these rules to keep it. And right away God has let them know that the abominations of the Canaanites, their worship of idols and the shedding of innocent blood, were the cause of their own destruction. God judges nations for these things.

Here specifically, God gives provision for an unsolved murder along the wayside or in the wilderness. If a body be found, slain, and the elders of the nearest city do not know who did it, they were to take a heifer and offer a sacrifice, washing their hands of the matter. This of course is an image of Christ, as all the sacrifices pictured, the washing of the hands to show innocence before God for the bloodshed is just as Pontius Pilate did.

As the Lord declared to Noah; *Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.*

**Proverbs 6:16-19**
*These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief, A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren.*

**Psalms 11:5**
*The LORD trieth the righteous: but the wicked and him that loveth violence his soul hateth.*

When a nation has refused to slay those who shed innocent blood, they are guilty of it. And God will repay. Be it repealing capital punishment, refusing to sentence a murderer to death, justifying or even funding abortions, bombing Innocents abroad, all these things bring judgment on a people, and the land will spew them out.

**Leviticus 18:28**
*That the land spew not you out also, when ye defile it, as it spewed out the nations that were before you.*

God requires of us that we stand against the shedding of innocent blood and seek His justice against those that do it.

teachings.title: Ye are the salt of the earth
teachings.summary: People are saved by faith alone, but nations are judged by Christians' works, so America's decline comes from believers losing their savour and not turning from wickedness, which is not persecution for righteousness' sake.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Psalm 37**, God promises that the wicked shall be cut down like grass, while those that trust in the Lord and do good shall dwell in the land and be fed.

This is a crucial detail in the Christian life, and the fate of our families and nation. The conditional understanding, that those who trust in the Lord, His people, the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus, are given the opportunity to have life, in abundance, though obedience to the commandments of God. To do good.

We are given eternal life by faith in Christ Jesus alone. Trusting God. But our lives on this earth are judged by the good that we do.

People are judged by faith. Nations are judged by Christians' works.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

It is a popular verse, quoted often from pulpits across America. And it shows that there is a solution to the chaos and depravity affecting our society, and that solution is not found in consuming political commentary or voting. It is turning towards God and away from evil, as His people.

**Matthew 5:13**
*Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men.*

Salt is a preservative that keeps meat from spoiling. It not only stops the rotting, but improves the flavor and texture of it when cooked. When tried by the fire.

We are to be that salt, and when the Christian loses his savour, we see that we become useless, and are left to be trodden down, and rightfully so.

This is in contrast with the earlier verse;

**Matthew 5:10–12**
*Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake. Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you.*

We often hear Christians complain about being vexed by the filthy conversation of the wicked, and who treat the inevitable trodding down caused by our lack of commitment and separation, as persecution for righteousness sake. They are not the same.

In fact, many Christians live as the world, not doing good that they may dwell in the land, and act surprised when the wicked prosper and our nation is flooded with strangers, bringing their idolatry and paganism with them.

They act as though they are being persecuted by politicians and corrupt leaders, while in reality we are the cause.

We become fearful and resentful, fretting about evildoers and being envious of the workers of iniquity.

We ignore God's prescriptions for what ails us, and so we forsake the promises of safety and provision He has given us.

teachings.title: No freedom of religion in the Kingdom
teachings.summary: Conversion comes by the word and never the sword, so the Baptist distinctive of freedom from state religion is right, churches should be local, independent and Christ led, and a godly people should not allow false religions to be practiced.
teachings.text:
There is no "freedom of religion" in the Kingdom of Heaven. There is a right to individuals to choose not to believe. No one can force conversion by the sword, only by the word. But the allowance and practice of false religions should never be allowed by a Christian people.

The Baptist Distinctive regarding freedom from state religion is good, and right. A secular denomination with political power to force conversions will always create false gospels and result in persecution of believers. Churches should be local and independent, Christ led. Not top-down controlled by men.

A nation of believers should enforce this rule, destroying cults that worship other gods and lead others to apostasy. In my opinion.

But to have such a thing requires a godly people. The blessings of liberty are only bestowed on a nation when a large enough portion are at liberty in Christ.

Idolatrous sects, pagans, Jews, satanic cults, perverse groups who seek after other gods, rejecting the God of our fathers, should never have been given the freedom to spread their abominations.

There was a time when our forefathers understood that. The same people who wrote and adopted the Bill of Rights did not allow antichrist religions. Or at least tried not to. They blew it, in the end. And our people turned from God and now we suffer as a nation for it, making the point moot.

But this will be enforced in the Millennium. Amen.

teachings.title: Seek the Lord while he may be found
teachings.summary: God is longsuffering, but there comes a point when He withdraws Himself from a nation or an individual and they become reprobate, so men must seek Him now while He may be found.
teachings.text:
The Lord is not happy with Israel. The priests and kings having led the people to ruin. Ephraim, Judah, Benjamin, all get named along with greater Israel for their condemnation.

Is there any judgment upon a nation as fearsome as their seeking the Lord and not being able to find Him, because He has withdrawn Himself from them?

**Jeremiah 6:30**
*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them*.

God is long-suffering, He is mercy that He will repent of evil He would do to a people if they turn from their wicked ways, and seek His face. But at some point, He will withdraw the offer, and allow His wrath to pour out on the wicked.

This is the same for individuals. Reprobation is real. The hour of salvation is here, now. Don't put it off. Seek Him while He can be found.

**Isaiah 55:6-7**
*Seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the Lord, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.*

**2 Corinthians 6:2**
*For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.*

**Matthew 13:14-15**
*And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive: For this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.*

teachings.title: The Lord hath made all things for himself
teachings.summary: God judges the spirit behind men's deeds and uses even the wicked, like Assyria, for His purposes, so we should commit our works to Him and walk in the fear of the Lord, which brings wisdom and makes even our enemies be at peace with us.
teachings.text:
Following the opening verse, we get a quick succession of proverbs that highlight the way of the Lord, and insight to His understanding.

The Lord judges the ways of a man by the spirit behind what we do. Men may justify every deed and word, but it is the intent and heart behind them that God cares about. A man can do good for bad reasons, he can do evil with good intentions. We do things in ignorance, we do things willfully, and so God judges righteous judgement, as only He can.

And so, to ensure we are walking in His ways, we are encouraged to commit our works to the Lord and our thoughts will be established. The spirit behind our deeds will be His, rather than our vain rationalizations.

The Lord has made all creation, everything that is, is His. Even the wicked who do evil serve a purpose for the Lord. Consider Assyria;

**Isaiah 10:1-6**
*Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees, and that write grievousness which they have prescribed; To turn aside the needy from judgment, and to take away the right from the poor of my people, that widows may be their prey, and that they may rob the fatherless! And what will ye do in the day of visitation, and in the desolation which shall come from far? to whom will ye flee for help? and where will ye leave your glory? Without me they shall bow down under the prisoners, and they shall fall under the slain. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still. O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger, and the staff in their hand is mine indignation. I will send him against an hypocritical nation, and against the people of my wrath will I give him a charge, to take the spoil, and to take the prey, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets.*

The destruction of the northern kingdom of Israel by the heathen empire was done by the wicked. Assyria is described as the rod of God's anger. Again the sovereignty and judgment of the Lord results in all things being for His purpose. Not determinism, but utility of the ultimate authority, towards His ends.

The proud of heart are an abomination to the Lord, even when they join forces against Him. I think of the armies Satan deceives into attacking Jesus and the camp of the saints at the end of the Millennial Kingdom, appealing to their pride. They unite for the battle of Gog and Magog, and are instantly destroyed, punished for their pride.

**Revelation 20:7-9**
*And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison, And shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog, and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea. And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them.*

As we have been instructed over and over again, fear of the Lord brings understanding and wisdom, wisdom brings mercy and love of truth, and these in practice purge iniquity and injustice from men.

By heeding the wisdom of the Lord, by seeking and walking in His paths, by acknowledging Him in all our ways, we please the Lord and rather than the destruction of the prideful and the visiting of evil, He will even make our enemies be at peace with us.

In **Genesis 26:28-29**, Isaac prospered and lived righteously, causing his chief enemy, King Abimelech, to come to him seeking a covenant of peace, acknowledging that God was with him.

This is most evident in the cycle of Judges.

**Judges 2:14-19**
*And the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of spoilers that spoiled them, and he sold them into the hands of their enemies round about, so that they could not any longer stand before their enemies. Whithersoever they went out, the hand of the Lord was against them for evil, as the Lord had said, and as the Lord had sworn unto them: and they were greatly distressed. Nevertheless the Lord raised up judges, which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them.*

teachings.title: The Lord pondereth the hearts
teachings.summary: God ordains rulers and directs the king's heart, and He judges the spirit behind men's deeds, valuing mercy and judgment over sacrifice, so the sacrifice of the wicked is abomination.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 21** adds to the sayings of the king, first hand advice of Solomon to his heir, that God is the master and commander of the ship of state, as He sets the heart of the king to His own devices.

Just as the Lord said of Pharaoh;

**Romans 9:17**
*For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.*

And the government is on the shoulders of whom its given;

**Romans 13:1**
*Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.*

What a humbling saying for a young prince to hear. For good or ill, God's anointed is ordained to power in His will and to the Almighty Lord's purpose.

*Every way of a man is right in his own eyes: but the Lord pondereth the hearts.* The spirit behind what a man does, this is what God judges. The things we do in sin aren't only those things that no good led to, fornication, iniquity, theft, deceit, covetousness...those aren't the only ways we sin and fall short. Often we can do the right things for the wrong reasons. God knows our hearts.

That's why, especially for a prince, to do justice and judgment, with fairness and right spirit, means more to God than sacrifice. As Jesus says to the Pharisees;

**Matthew 9:13**
*But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance*.

This, quoting **Hosea 6:6**
*For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.*

This leads to a theme of the heart of the wicked. Their tendencies and traits.

The high look and proud heart of the wicked, their plans and schemes, this is sin. Diligence has a reward, haste leads to want.

Lying for wealth is a vanity, the wise king says, and it is passed back and forth between thieves, those that seek death and not life. There is no honor among thieves. Their robberies end in death. They are destroyed by their ways. They refuse judgment. Everything they seek to gain is motivated by greed and covetousness. Their way is froward and strange. But for the pure, those seeking to walk on God's path, their work is right.

The wicked desires evil. They do not love even their neighbors, violating even the second great command.

**Matthew 22:37-39**
*Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.*

In the end, God will overthrow the wicked for their wickedness. The wicked ignore the cries of the poor, and so God will not hear the wicked's cry.

Their love of pleasure results in poverty, that lack of impulse control. High time preference. This will ruin a man led by his own desires. A foolish man spends all he has.

Scorners are proud and haughty, their wrath comes from their pride. Overreacting to slights. Their pride insulted.

The lazy are their own destruction, the slothful kills themselves by their lack of labor. Their end is hunger. They shall always want.

The covetous, often the same foolish, lazy, proud and unjust fool, the robber, he who hates his neighbor, they are consumed by their greed all day long.

God promises the false witness will perish, and the wicked is set in their ways.

Tying this thread all back together to the beginning, we are given the understanding God judges hearts, the spirit of the man, and He values mercy and judgement over sacrifice, we see then the truth; *The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?*

teachings.title: Why do the heathen rage
teachings.summary: Psalm 2 prophesies the rulers' vain rebellion against God's anointed, whom God raised up and set as King over the nations, warning rulers to kiss the Son and trust in Him.
teachings.text:
Why do the heathen rage? Why do people think they can go against God? Kings and rulers, presidents and prime ministers, popes and priests, all seek to be freed from the ways of the Lord, to do what they will.

Especially the religious and political leaders in the time of Jesus.

**Acts 4:27**
*For of a truth against thy holy child Jesus, whom thou hast anointed, both Herod, and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles, and the people of Israel, were gathered together*.

They believed if they killed the Son, they would break the bands, Their bonds, and be free of God.

Jesus addressed this in a parable, about a Lord who planted a vineyard and lent it out to husbandmen to dress and keep it. And when the Lord sent servants to gather the harvest, the stewards beat and killed them. So finally, the Lord sends his son;

**Matthew 21:38**
*But when the husbandmen saw the son, they said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and let us seize on his inheritance*.

David prophetically writes of this here in **Psalm 2**.

But, it is folly. The Lord holds them in derision. He laughs at their vain efforts, because Christ, His anointed, rose again.

He set His Son upon Zion, and upon the throne.

**Acts 13:32–33**
*And we declare unto you glad tidings, how that the promise which was made unto the fathers, God hath fulfilled the same unto us their children, in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee.*

Jesus' inheritance are all the nations of the world, and possession of the uttermost parts of the world. And as Lord of lords and King of kings, He will rule them.

**Revelation 2:26–27**
*And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers: even as I received of my Father.*

This prophetic Psalm gives warning to the rulers of this world, reminding them of their place. That they serve at the pleasure of the Lord, and He will deliver vengeance.

It's an amazing and consistent message, across the entire Bible; The Christ is God's anointed, and Jesus is the Christ. All who believe on Christ Jesus shall be saved. His grace and mercy giving us the chance to serve Him in righteousness.

*Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling. Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and ye perish from the way, when his wrath is kindled but a little. Blessed are all they that put their trust in him.*

Amen
